sheet-73.description: Sheet 73 shows the southernmost oceanfront blocks of Belmar, between 20th Avenue and 17th Avenue, from B Street down to Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean. The sheet is turned on the page so that the avenues run up it, Ocean Avenue and the shore lie along the bottom, and north points to the right. Seven blocks, numbered 2 to 8 across the sheet, are drawn as narrow numbered lots running back from the avenues; the numbers are printed in every lot but almost none of the land is built on. Blocks 2 and 3 between B Street and A Street are open land cut by a diagonal property line, with a small row of lots at their lower edge. Block 4, between 18th and 17th Avenues, carries the only buildings, a fishing station with two small sheds at its lower right corner. The blocks between A Street and Ocean Avenue, 5, 6 and 7, are divided into rows of lots ending in a tier of narrow beach lots next to Ocean Avenue. The ocean and a wavy shoreline fill the bottom margin, with the compass, the scale bar of 60 feet to an inch and a Princeton Map Division stamp. Neighbouring sheet numbers 74, 80 and others are printed at the sheet edges.
notes: Fishing station in block 4 near 17th Avenue and A Street.
Modern 19th Avenue meets B Street about 44 m from where the 1905 sheet draws it; that junction was left out.
Oceanfront, 20th to 17th Avenue, B Street to Ocean Avenue; 60 ft; north to the right. 19th Avenue / B Street excluded (modern node 44 m from the drawn junction).

sheet-74.description: Sheet 74 covers Belmar's oceanfront between 17th Avenue and 13th Avenue, from B Street down to Ocean Avenue and the beach. The sheet is turned so that the avenues run up the page, Ocean Avenue lies along the bottom and north points to the right. Eight blocks, numbered 1 to 8, are drawn. The four blocks between B Street and A Street are subdivided into narrow numbered lots and hold little: block 4 has a laundry, the Salvation Army Building described as a staff home and rest, and several small dwellings near 13th Avenue. The four blocks between A Street and Ocean Avenue hold the large seaside hotels: Hotel Neptune with servants quarters, dressing rooms and a water tank on block 8, the Atlantic Hotel with a kitchen, shed and wind pump on block 7, and Hotel Colorado, a cross shaped building with kitchen and water tank, on block 6. Block 5 has a smaller building and sheds near the beach. The hotel notes record watchman, power, heat and lights. A board walk runs along the shore beyond Ocean Avenue, water pipes are marked along the avenues, and the compass, ocean and scale bar of 60 feet to an inch fill the bottom margin.
notes: Hotel Neptune, Atlantic Hotel and Hotel Colorado stand between A Street and Ocean Avenue.
Salvation Army Building, staff home and rest, on block 4.
Oceanfront, 17th to 13th Avenue, B Street to Ocean Avenue; 60 ft; north to the right.

sheet-75.description: Sheet 75 covers the oceanfront blocks of Belmar between 13th Avenue and 10th Avenue, from B Street down to Ocean Avenue and the beach. The sheet is turned on the page: the avenues run up the sheet, Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean lie along the bottom, and north points to the right. Six blocks are drawn, numbered 1 to 6, each divided into narrow lots running back from the avenues with lot numbers printed in every lot. The blocks between B Street and A Street are mostly vacant lots with scattered frame dwellings, more of them towards 10th and 11th Avenues. The blocks between A Street and Ocean Avenue hold larger frame cottages and, along the ocean front, the Hotel Delaware and the Belmar Summer Club House between 13th and 12th Avenues and The Melrose Inn with its annex between 11th and 10th Avenues. Seaward of Ocean Avenue the board walk runs the length of the sheet, and the W. S. Jackson Bathing Pavilion with bath houses, board rooms and a summer restaurant stands on the beach opposite 11th Avenue. Water pipes are marked along the avenues and Ocean Avenue, with fire hydrants at several corners. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch; the shoreline and the ocean fill the lower margin, with a north arrow and the scale bar.
notes: Hotel Delaware, Belmar Summer Club House and The Melrose Inn face Ocean Avenue.
W. S. Jackson Bathing Pavilion on the beach opposite 11th Avenue, with a board walk along the whole front.
Oceanfront, 13th to 10th Avenue, B Street to Ocean Avenue; 60 ft; turned (north to the right). Pilot sheet.

sheet-76.description: Sheet 76 shows the built up oceanfront blocks of Belmar between 10th Avenue and 7th Avenue, from B Street to Ocean Avenue. The sheet is turned so that the avenues run up the page, the ocean lies along the bottom and north points to the right. Six blocks, numbered 1 to 6, are drawn as narrow lots with frame dwellings, outbuildings and stables scattered through them. Block 1, between 10th and 9th Avenues above A Street, contains Barkalow's Boarding and Livery with a wagon shed, hen house, carriage house and a water tank with wind pump. Block 5, between 9th and 8th Avenues below A Street, has the Hotel Carleton, marked as having no heat, with lights of gas and electricity and no admission without a caretaker, and several dwellings near Ocean Avenue. Block 6 and block 4 have scattered dwellings, wells and barns. Ocean Avenue runs along the bottom with a wide board walk and water pipes marked beyond it, then the beach, the shore and the Atlantic Ocean, with the compass and the scale bar of 60 feet to an inch. Neighbouring sheet numbers 75 and 77 are printed on the sides.
notes: Barkalow's Boarding and Livery on block 1; Hotel Carleton on block 5.
Water pipes of 4 inch and 6 inch are lettered along the avenues and Ocean Avenue.
Oceanfront, 10th to 7th Avenue, B Street to Ocean Avenue; 60 ft; north to the right.

sheet-77.description: Sheet 77 shows the oceanfront of Belmar between 7th Avenue and 4th Avenue, divided in the middle by Silver Lake, which fills the upper centre of the sheet with the main street grid on either side. The sheet is turned so that the avenues run up the page, Ocean Avenue is near the bottom and north points to the right. On the left, blocks 1 and 5 are cut by the curving lake shore and a diagonal street along it, with scattered frame dwellings and The Summer Tabernacle at the corner of A Street. In the lower centre, block 4 lies between the foot of the lake and Ocean Avenue, with Bennett's Automobile and Carriage Repair Shop of fireproof construction and a few sheds. On the right, blocks 2 and 3, between 5th and 4th Avenues, hold dwellings, Hotel Windsor at the top of block 2 and Hotel Brunswick in block 3, each with a note on heat and lights. Along the shore a board walk runs beyond Ocean Avenue, and Gordon's Bathing Pavilion with boards, bath houses and a restaurant stands on the beach. Neighbouring sheets 76, 78, 84 and 85 are printed at the edges. The scale is 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Silver Lake interrupts A Street and B Street; the junctions of 6th Avenue with A Street and with the lake shore were left out of the control.
The lake shore street is lettered S. Lake Av.; the modern streets there are South Lake Drive and North Lake Avenue.
Modern 5th Avenue and A Street junction lies about 7 m from the position the sheet draws and was rejected.
Oceanfront, 7th to 4th Avenue, with the east end of Silver Lake and S. Lake Av.; 60 ft; north to the right. 6th Avenue / A Street excluded (lake); lake streets left out.

sheet-78.description: Sheet 78 covers Belmar's oceanfront between 4th Avenue and 1st Avenue, from B Street down to Ocean Avenue. The sheet is turned so that the avenues run up the page, Ocean Avenue and the shore are along the bottom and north points to the right. Six blocks are drawn. Blocks 1 and 2, between B Street and A Street, hold mainly frame dwellings and outbuildings, with the Llanamore Hotel and its annex at the lower left of block 2. Block 3, at the right, is cut diagonally by a street line and has a few dwellings. Blocks 5 and 6 below A Street hold the larger hotels: the Columbia Hotel, with power, steam and electric plant, kitchen and laundry, the Buena Vista Hotel with its annex and servants quarters, and a group of frame cottages. Block 4 at the lower right is a triangular block bounded by a diagonal street, with several dwellings. Water pipes run along the avenues. The board walk follows the shore beyond Ocean Avenue, and a pier marked 600 feet in length runs into the ocean at the right edge. The compass, ocean and scale bar of 60 feet to an inch fill the bottom.
notes: Llanamore Hotel, Columbia Hotel and Buena Vista Hotel with annex are the largest buildings.
A pier of 600 feet runs from the board walk at the right edge.
Oceanfront, 4th to 1st Avenue at the Shark River inlet; 60 ft; north to the right.

sheet-79.description: Sheet 79 shows the western, thinly built part of Belmar around the New York and Long Branch Railroad, between 16th Avenue and 13th Avenue. Unlike the beach sheets it shows a street grid along F Street, with the railroad running across the top of the sheet and the compass above it; north points to the right. Two lettered and numbered blocks, 2 and 3, lie between the railroad and F Street, divided into numbered lots with a few dwellings, a carpenter shop and a tin shop with a plumber. Below F Street a row of lots, with an old wagon house, forms the top of block 4, which otherwise is open ground with scattered dwellings along 16th Avenue and an irregular lot pattern. On the left block 1 holds a planing mill with an engine, a paint, wood work and blacksmith shop and a carriage house, marked no lights and no fire apparatus; Jeffery Avenue is lettered along the diagonal edge. Block 5, at the lower left, contains the Seaside Hotel and a bar, ice houses and a foundation. A road runs diagonally at the right edge. Scale is 60 feet to an inch.
notes: F Street is today Main Street. The avenue lettered 14th here lies where modern 15th Avenue crosses Main Street, so it was matched to that junction.
The road at the right edge shows only the end of its name, ending in Road; it was left out.
Planing mill, Seaside Hotel and the wagon house (old) are the named works.

West of the railroad, F Street (Main Street) from 13th to 16th Avenue and Jeffery Avenue; 60 ft; north to the right. Control only along Main Street; the avenue lettered 14th matched to modern 15th Avenue by spacing.

sheet-80.description: Sheet 80 covers a thinly built tract on the south-western side of Belmar, along 16th Avenue between B Street and the area towards the railroad. The sheet is turned on the page so that north points to the right: 16th Avenue runs down the sheet from top to bottom, and B Street runs across the bottom edge, where 15th, 14th and 13th Avenues meet it. Only the lots along B Street are laid out and numbered; the rest of the sheet is open ground in large blocks numbered 3, 4 and 5. Scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings stand along both sides of 16th Avenue, most of them near the top of the sheet, where a row of numbered lots with dwellings, a fish house and a grocery faces the avenue. On the west side, in block 5, is a poultry farm with its office and sheds. In block 4 east of 16th Avenue are about a dozen dwellings with their outbuildings. New Bedford Road crosses the lower left corner diagonally towards B Street. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, with its north arrow and scale bar near the bottom; most of its area is blank paper.
notes: Placed from four junctions along B Street (helmert): position and rotation rest on one street; medium to low confidence.
Poultry farm in block 5 west of 16th Avenue.
Open tract along 16th Avenue west of B Street, 13th to 16th Avenue at B Street; 60 ft; north to the right. Only junctions are along B Street (helmert).

sheet-81.description: Sheet 81 covers a block-and-lot grid in the middle of Belmar between 9th Avenue at the top and 13th Avenue at the bottom, and from F Street on the left to D Street on the right. The sheet is drawn with north roughly up, tilted a few degrees, and the compass rose sits in the lower middle. Eight numbered blocks are shown, each cut into narrow lots with lot numbers printed in them. Development is concentrated at the west (left) side near F Street: the First National Bank building with offices, a barber, laundry and bakery in the northwest block, Heiler's Villa and a group of frame dwellings in the block between 10th and 11th Avenues, and, between 11th and 12th Avenues, a blacksmith shop, a wheelwright and the Volunteer Hook and Ladder company house. The Union Fire Co. engine and hose house stands in the top right block facing 9th Avenue, and most other blocks to the east have only scattered dwellings on largely vacant lots, one street marked Not Opened. In the lower left block a Memorial Baptist Church and several cottages stand, including Forest Cottage, and a wide diagonal road cuts across the southwest corner of the sheet below 12th Avenue. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 12 inches are marked along the avenues and F Street, with fire hydrants and a fire alarm box at the corner of 10th Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: F Street is Main Street today.
A wide diagonal road crosses the lower left; only the word Road is printed beside it, so its name is not given.
The compass rose shows north tilted about 15 degrees from the top of the sheet; the fit rotation is about -15 degrees.
9th to 13th Avenue, F Street (Main Street) to D Street; 60 ft; north to the top (rotation about -15).

sheet-82.description: Sheet 82 lies east of sheet 81 and covers the grid of Belmar between 9th Avenue at the top and 13th Avenue at the bottom, from D Street on the left through C Street to B Street on the right. North is roughly up, with the compass rose in the lower left. Seven numbered blocks are drawn, divided into long narrow lots whose numbers are printed in each lot. The area is thinly built: most blocks hold a scattering of frame dwellings, some with open first-floor porches, and a good many lots are vacant, especially in the middle blocks and at the left. Houses are strung along the north side of 12th Avenue in the lower block, and a few small outbuildings and a laundry stand near D Street. A fire alarm box is marked at the corner of 10th Avenue and the right-hand street, and fire hydrants stand along the avenues. The lower part of the sheet is occupied by one large block, number 4, with an irregular boundary where a diagonal line cuts across the block towards the right, and a street at the right edge is marked Not Opened. A dashed box near 13th Avenue at the bottom right outlines an unbuilt lot. Water pipes of 4 inches run along the avenues. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and carries the word Belmar across the top.
notes: A street at the right edge of the lower block is marked Not Opened.
The compass rose shows north tilted about 15 degrees from the top of the sheet; the fit rotation is about -15 degrees.
9th to 13th Avenue, D Street to B Street; 60 ft; north to the top.

sheet-83.description: Sheet 83 covers the town centre of Belmar from 5th Avenue at the top to 9th Avenue at the bottom, between F Street on the left and D Street on the right. North is roughly up, with the compass rose at the right edge below 8th Avenue. Eight numbered blocks are shown. The west half, along F Street, is the most built-up part: dwellings, vacant-lot frames, a dry goods store, a drug store, furniture and hardware stores (P. C. Taylor, Hardware and Furniture), The Girard, a laundry, a lumber pile and board-yard sheds, and a collector's office along the F Street fronts. In the middle blocks between E Street and F Street stand St. Rose's Church with St. Rose's Church Hall (between 7th and 8th Avenues) and, at the bottom, the 1st Presbyn. Church. East of E Street the blocks are mostly vacant lots divided into narrow numbered lots with scattered frame dwellings and a few chicken coops and a wash house. The 1st M.E. Church, drawn in pink as a brick building, stands near D Street between 7th and 8th Avenues. A curved street marked N. Lake Av. runs off the right edge near the compass, towards Silver Lake. Fire alarm boxes, fire hydrants and 4, 6 and 12 inch water pipes are marked. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: F Street is Main Street today.
North Lake Avenue (printed N. Lake Av.) curves along the right edge towards Silver Lake and is not used for control.
The compass rose shows north tilted about 15 degrees from the top of the sheet; the fit rotation is about -15 degrees.
5th to 9th Avenue, F Street (Main Street) to D Street; 60 ft; north to the top. N. Lake Av. not used (curved).

sheet-84.description: Sheet 84 is dominated by Silver Lake, which fills the centre of the sheet as a blue-washed water body whose shores run diagonally from the upper right to the lower left. The sheet runs from 5th Avenue at the top to 9th Avenue at the bottom, between D Street on the left and B Street on the right, with C Street in the upper and lower middle. North is roughly up; the compass rose stands on the lake at the upper right. Streets and blocks stop at the shoreline: N. Lake Av. runs along the northwest shore, and the blocks beside it are cut off by diagonal lines. Development is sparse. The blocks in the upper left (between D and C Streets, 5th to 7th Avenues) hold a few frame dwellings and two small outbuildings on narrow numbered lots, and the block at the upper right between C Street and the lake has dwellings and a larger house with grounds. At the right, a block between 7th and 8th Avenues has several dwellings and a stable. At the bottom, between 8th and 9th Avenues, stand the 1st Baptist Church (Colored), a club house and block house, a few dwellings and a stretch of vacant lots. Fire alarm boxes, hydrants and 4 and 8 inch water pipes are marked along the avenues. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and has the word Belmar printed across the top.
notes: North Lake Avenue (printed N. Lake Av.) follows the northwest shore of Silver Lake and is not used for control.
Control is thin on this sheet: many junctions lie in or beside the lake or at the sheet edge.
The compass rose shows north tilted about 15 degrees from the top of the sheet; the fit rotation is about -16 degrees.
5th to 9th Avenue, D Street to B Street, Silver Lake in the middle; 60 ft; north to the top; thin control, many boundary points.

sheet-85.description: Sheet 85 shows the Shark River shore of Belmar, with the sheet turned so that north points to the right and the river runs down the right-hand side. The avenues run up and down the page (5th Avenue at the left, then 4th Avenue and 3rd Avenue), the lettered streets D, C and B cross them from top to bottom, and River Av. follows the curving shore on the right. Six numbered blocks are laid out in long narrow lots with numbers printed in each. Much of the upper part of the sheet beyond D Street is unlotted marsh bordering the Shark River, where the river widens into a bay at the top; further right the Main Shark River runs in a narrow channel down the sheet, with marsh on both sides. The built-up blocks hold frame dwellings, small outbuildings and a few larger buildings: the Clyde Hotel and The Protestant Episc. Summer Church (frame, no heat and no lights) at the left, The Cedar Ho. with studio, laundry and servants' quarters, and the Skidmore and Combs Columbia Hotel with boarding and livery stables in the blocks towards the river. Water tanks, a windmill pump house and 4 and 6 inch water pipes are marked, with fire hydrants at several corners. The compass rose lies on the river at the right. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: River Avenue here is the shore road along the Shark River, today River Road.
The sheet is turned: north points to the right of the page (fit rotation about 75 degrees).
D Street ends at 5th Avenue today; 4th and 3rd Avenues have no D Street junction.
Shark River shore, 3rd to 5th Avenue, B Street to D Street and River Avenue (River Road); 60 ft; north to the right.

sheet-86-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 86, drawn at 60 feet to an inch across the lower half of the sheet and turned on the page so that north points to the right. It covers the north-west corner of Belmar along the Shark River: the ends of 7th, 6th and 5th Avenues between the New York and Long Branch Railroad and F Street, with River Avenue running diagonally along the river bank from 6th Avenue down to F Street and 5th Avenue. Block 1, between 7th and 6th Avenues, holds the W. M. Bergen boarding and livery stables with a carriage house and carriage shed, a few dwellings and stores, and vacant lots towards the railroad. Block 2, between 6th Avenue and River Avenue, has a bakery (vacant), Pyott's auto garage and machine shop, stores and a dwelling near F Street, and an ice house of the Belmar Casino. On the river side of River Avenue stand the Basket Ball Hall and storage, storage and help quarters, and the large Belmar Summer Casino, built on driven piles at the water's edge with a saloon open in winter. At the right edge the street railway bridge and the county bridge cross the Shark River at 5th Avenue. The railroad crosses the top of the part with the river beside it. Water pipes are marked in F Street and the avenues, with a fire alarm box and hydrants. The upper half of the sheet holds two separate parts at 120 feet to an inch.
notes: F Street is now Main Street; the drawn River Avenue along the bank is the line of today's River Road.
Belmar Summer Casino and Basket Ball Hall stand on piles at the river edge; street railway bridge and county bridge at 5th Avenue.

Three parts. Part 1 (lower half, 60 ft): 7th to 5th Avenue at F Street (Main Street) and River Avenue on the Shark River. Part 2 (upper left, 120 ft): 16th Avenue, River Avenue and Wall Road west of Camp Belmar, hotels; one junction (anchored). Part 3 (upper right, 120 ft): Camp Belmar (Maplewood Road, Pine Tree Way, Brierwood Road) and L/K Streets, 16th to 13th Avenue.

sheet-86-2.description: Part 2 is the upper left part of sheet 86, set off by heavy lines and drawn at 120 feet to an inch, with north pointing to the right. It shows the country west of Camp Belmar on the south bank of the Shark River, where Wall Road and the road towards New Bedford (marked one and a half miles to the New Bedford Hotel) meet 16th Avenue and River Avenue. 16th Avenue runs along the left side of the part and River Avenue runs diagonally beside the river, which crosses the part from top to bottom. Three hotels are drawn: the Willow Gem Hotel of C. King at the junction of Wall Road, with a wind pump and water tank, a hen house and outbuildings; Ribles Hotel on River Avenue; and the Hotel Luray with its servants' quarters and stables on a large lot further along River Avenue. Each carries notes on power, heat, lights and fire apparatus. The rest of the part is open land in large blocks numbered 9, 10 and 11. Although drawn on the page beside Camp Belmar, the part lies further west along 16th Avenue, and its border is the heavy line shared with parts 1 and 3.
notes: Wall Road is today's Belmar Boulevard; River Avenue here is the line of today's River Road.
Placed from a single junction (16th Avenue / River Road) at the configured 120 ft scale: low confidence.
Willow Gem Hotel, Ribles Hotel and Hotel Luray.

Three parts. Part 1 (lower half, 60 ft): 7th to 5th Avenue at F Street (Main Street) and River Avenue on the Shark River. Part 2 (upper left, 120 ft): 16th Avenue, River Avenue and Wall Road west of Camp Belmar, hotels; one junction (anchored). Part 3 (upper right, 120 ft): Camp Belmar (Maplewood Road, Pine Tree Way, Brierwood Road) and L/K Streets, 16th to 13th Avenue.

sheet-86-3.description: Part 3 is the upper right part of sheet 86, set off by heavy lines and drawn at 120 feet to an inch, with north pointing to the right. It covers the Camp Belmar tract between 16th Avenue and the Shark River, west of the town, and the blocks between L Street and K Street from 16th Avenue to River Avenue. Camp Belmar is laid out with Maplewood Road, Pine Tree Way and Brierwood Road running from 16th Avenue to River Avenue, the lots fanning around a circle on Pine Tree Way; the name Camp Belmar is lettered around it. Nearly every lot is numbered and almost all are vacant. At the river end of Pine Tree Way stands the Rhode Island Point Inn of R. G. Clayton, with a note that all buildings are to be moved to conform with the street, and a few small buildings nearby. Below L Street the blocks between 16th, 14th and 13th Avenues and River Avenue are divided into lots with a handful of dwellings and a stable near 13th Avenue. The Shark River runs down the right edge of the part. K Street forms the bottom edge, where sheet 89 continues.
notes: Brierwood Road is today's Briarwood Road; River Avenue is today's River Road.
Rhode Island Point Inn, R. G. Clayton proprietor, with buildings to be moved to conform with the street.

Three parts. Part 1 (lower half, 60 ft): 7th to 5th Avenue at F Street (Main Street) and River Avenue on the Shark River. Part 2 (upper left, 120 ft): 16th Avenue, River Avenue and Wall Road west of Camp Belmar, hotels; one junction (anchored). Part 3 (upper right, 120 ft): Camp Belmar (Maplewood Road, Pine Tree Way, Brierwood Road) and L/K Streets, 16th to 13th Avenue.

sheet-87.description: Sheet 87 covers the Shark River edge of Belmar around the railroad, drawn with north to the right of the page, so that the avenues run up the sheet (13th Avenue at the left, then 12th, 11th and 10th Avenues) and H Street and F Street cross it at the top and bottom. The N.Y. & Long Branch R.R. runs across the middle of the sheet as a bundle of parallel tracks with a freight house beside it. North of the tracks, the Belmar Water Works stands at 12th Avenue with its pump room, coal bins and a 60,000 gallon water tank, and Allen's Hay, Straw, Coal and Wood yard with storage, open coal bins and a wood pile occupies a block to the east. Along River Av., which follows the curved shore of the Shark River at the top right, are a boat house, the Belmar Club House with a boat building and an ice cream shop, and scattered dwellings on narrow lots. Bay View Av. crosses the upper left blocks, which are mostly vacant lots with a few dwellings. South of the tracks the blocks are divided into long numbered lots; one block at the lower left is noted as all buildings dilapidated and not used within the past 8 or 10 years, and holds a vacant mill with boiler room and a shed destroyed by fire. The Belmar Public School, drawn in pink as a brick building, stands in the middle block against F Street. The compass rose is on the river at the upper right, and the sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: F Street is Main Street today, and H Street here is Route 71.
Bay View Av. is Bayview Avenue today.
River Avenue here is the shore road along the Shark River, today River Road; it is not used for control.
The sheet is turned: north points to the right of the page (fit rotation about 74 degrees).
10th to 13th Avenue, H Street (Route 71) to F Street (Main Street) across the railroad, Bay View Avenue, Shark River; 60 ft; north to the right.

sheet-88-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 88, drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the right. It covers the business blocks of Belmar around the railroad station between 10th Avenue and 7th Avenue, from F Street up across the New York and Long Branch Railroad to River Avenue and the Shark River. Beside the railroad stand the Belmar R. R. Station with a news stand and baggage room, and two small parks laid out in front of it between 10th and 9th Avenues. Block 6 holds the Belmar post office, Bennett's Athletic Hall, Bennett's auto station and machine works and a row of stores on F Street. The block between 9th and 8th Avenues has The European House with a bowling alley at the railroad end, a printing room, Adams Express office, an ice house, a drug store and a building being built on F Street. The block between 8th and 7th Avenues has dwellings, stores, a bakery and George B. Kisner's blacksmith and carriage shop. North of the railroad three blocks lie along River Avenue, mostly vacant, with dwellings, the United Ice Company's ice house and its office. In the upper left corner a pier runs out into the Shark River to Buhler's Pavilion. A heavy line cuts off the upper right of the sheet, which holds a separate part drawn along H Street.
notes: F Street is now Main Street; River Avenue is today's River Road.
Belmar R. R. Station on the New York and Long Branch Railroad (today's North Jersey Coast Line), with the post office, The European House and Bennett's Athletic Hall nearby.

Two parts, 60 ft, north to the right. Part 1: 10th to 7th Avenue from F Street (Main Street) across the railroad to River Avenue, station and post office. Part 2 (upper right, behind a heavy line): H Street (Route 71) between Walling, Jeffery (17th) and Middle (Curtis) Avenues south of 16th Avenue; helmert.

sheet-88-2.description: Part 2 fills the upper right of sheet 88 above a heavy dividing line and is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north pointing to the right, like the rest of the sheet. On the ground it lies well south-west of the main part: it shows H Street, the old Manasquan Turnpike, south of 16th Avenue, where Walling Avenue, Jeffery Avenue and Middle Avenue cross it on the western edge of Belmar. H Street runs across the part from left to right, with Walling Avenue crossing at an angle, Jeffery Avenue in the middle and Middle Avenue at the right edge, where sheet 89 continues. The blocks, numbered 7 to 11, are large and thinly built, with frame dwellings, a store, sheds, hen houses and stables facing H Street and Jeffery Avenue; most of block 7 is open land. The lower edge of the part follows the Shark River, which the dividing line crosses diagonally, so the river bank itself is drawn in the main part below. Street widths are marked: 50 feet for Jeffery Avenue, 40 feet for Middle Avenue and 35 to 45 feet for H Street.
notes: H Street here is today's Route 71; Jeffery Avenue is today's 17th Avenue and Middle Avenue today's Curtis Avenue (identified by position along Route 71).
Placed from three junctions along one street (helmert): low to medium confidence.

Two parts, 60 ft, north to the right. Part 1: 10th to 7th Avenue from F Street (Main Street) across the railroad to River Avenue, station and post office. Part 2 (upper right, behind a heavy line): H Street (Route 71) between Walling, Jeffery (17th) and Middle (Curtis) Avenues south of 16th Avenue; helmert.

sheet-89-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 89, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the top, unlike most sheets of this atlas. It covers the western edge of Belmar along H Street from 13th Avenue south past 14th Avenue and 16th Avenue to Middle Avenue, with K Street at the left edge and the New York and Long Branch Railroad along the right edge. K Street and 14th Avenue west of H Street are marked as not opened. Most of the area is large, thinly built blocks. The large block 1 between H Street, 13th Avenue, 16th Avenue and the railroad is mostly vacant; at its railroad side stand G. P. Farmer's Coal and Supply Company with wood and hay storage and open coal bins on a siding, and the Coast Gas Company's Belmar plant with its main and relief gasometers, oil tank, generating and boiler rooms and purifying building. At the corner of H Street and 16th Avenue are the West Belmar Hotel and S. Michelsohn's wholesale and retail liquor business with a bottling establishment and a rectifying plant; across H Street is the Stratford Inn with its annex. Dwellings, wagon sheds and stables are scattered over the blocks south of 16th Avenue towards Middle Avenue. The sheet bears a stamped date of July 1905. The lower right corner is a separate inset of River Avenue.
notes: H Street here is today's Route 71; Middle Avenue is today's Curtis Avenue.
Coast Gas Company's Belmar plant and G. P. Farmer's Coal and Supply Company beside the railroad.
West Belmar Hotel, S. Michelsohn liquors and the Stratford Inn on H Street at 16th Avenue.

Two parts, 60 ft, north to the top. Part 1: H Street (Route 71) from 13th Avenue to Middle Avenue (Curtis), gas works and coal yard by the railroad. Part 2 (lower right inset): block between River Avenue, K Street, H Street and 13th Avenue; anchored on one hand-picked junction. Scan is stained grey; ink_below_paper 80 on both parts.

sheet-89-2.description: Part 2 is an inset in the lower right corner of sheet 89, set off by a heavy line and drawn at 60 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, turned a few degrees from the main part. It shows a single block, numbered 4, between River Avenue and 13th Avenue from K Street to H Street, on the south bank of the Shark River west of the town. The block is divided into numbered lots facing River Avenue and 13th Avenue. It is vacant except for a frame building in course of erection near H Street. The Shark River runs along the top of the inset beyond River Avenue, just inside the heavy border. Street widths of 60 and 80 feet are marked. The inset continues the Camp Belmar area of sheet 86 to the north and lies just north of the main part of this sheet.
notes: River Avenue is today's River Road.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (13th Avenue / K Street) with a set scale and rotation: low confidence.

Two parts, 60 ft, north to the top. Part 1: H Street (Route 71) from 13th Avenue to Middle Avenue (Curtis), gas works and coal yard by the railroad. Part 2 (lower right inset): block between River Avenue, K Street, H Street and 13th Avenue; anchored on one hand-picked junction. Scan is stained grey; ink_below_paper 80 on both parts.
